drafts.title: Front seats: longer thigh support, lasting cushion comfort and reliable memory restore
drafts.description: Tall drivers can extend front seat thigh support and keep a consistent, supportive cushion feel over years; saved seat positions are restored reliably every time.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Front seats provide at least 80 mm of adjustable thigh-support extension; seat-cushion compressed thickness retains >=85% of its original thickness after an equivalent of 100,000 usage cycles (laboratory durability test); and saved seating positions are restored within ±2 cm linear and ±2° angular deviation on at least 99 out of 100 memory recalls.
assumptions: Industry-standard seat durability protocol exists to simulate 100,000 cycles and measure compressed thickness.
80 mm extension is achievable within current vehicle packaging for the 5 Series successor without degrading other ergonomics.
Seat memory system can store position offsets per user and retain them across power cycles.
uncertainties: Actual long-term wear depends on user weight distribution and usage patterns.
Achieving both large adjustable range and high long-term durability may require material or design trade-offs affecting seat weight or cost.

drafts.title: Cup holders that fit common bottles and travel mugs
drafts.description: Cup holders accept and secure common bottled beverages and popular travel mugs without needing adapters.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Cup holders accept cylindrical vessels up to 90 mm diameter and retain them securely under 0.3 g lateral acceleration in a standardized fixture; in a 100-sample fit test using market bottles and travel mugs, fit rate must be 100%.
assumptions: 90 mm covers the large majority of common travel mugs and 1.5 L bottle base diameters found in the US market.
Retention test at 0.3 g represents typical cornering loads for passenger comfort testing.
uncertainties: Some very large aftermarket tumblers may exceed 90 mm and will not be accommodated.

drafts.title: Hands-free tailgate opens reliably on the first attempt
drafts.description: Customers can open the hands-free tailgate with a single, natural gesture without repeated attempts.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: First-attempt open success rate of at least 95% measured over 100 consecutive real-user trials using standard foot gestures performed at 20–50 cm from the bumper, across at least 10 different users, with trunk load up to 20 kg.
assumptions: Trials are conducted on dry pavement and normal footwear; extreme footwear (e.g., very thick-soled snow boots) are excluded.
Users perform a single deliberate foot motion in front of the center of the bumper.
uncertainties: Performance may degrade with heavy bumper dirt/icing or when users stand outside the 20–50 cm window.

drafts.title: Flush door handles operate reliably in freezing conditions
drafts.description: Flush door handles open on the first try in cold and icy weather so customers can access the car without manual intervention or damage.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: After exposure to -10°C ambient conditions and up to 3 mm of ice accretion in a controlled freeze-thaw lab test, flush door handles must operate on the first attempt in at least 98% of 50 test cycles.
assumptions: -10°C and 3 mm ice represent typical severe winter conditions in many US markets; harsher conditions may require additional measures.
Test includes salt contamination representative of winter road use.
uncertainties: Extreme ice thicknesses or prolonged sub-zero exposure may still impair operation and could require active de-icing measures.

drafts.title: Ambient lighting with expanded color palette and brightness steps
drafts.description: Customers can personalise interior ambient lighting with many distinct colors and fine-grained brightness control saved to their user profile.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: System offers at least 64 distinct colors and 10 discrete brightness levels per lighting zone, with chosen color/brightness saved to the user's profile and applied within 1 second of selection.
assumptions: LED and control hardware can support 64-color mixing per zone within cost targets.
User profiles persist across vehicle power cycles.
uncertainties: Perceived color accuracy can vary with interior trim materials and viewing angles.

drafts.title: Rear seating: legroom at or above competitive class benchmarks
drafts.description: Rear passengers enjoy legroom that matches or exceeds main competitors in the executive sedan class.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Rear knee clearance of at least 900 mm measured from the rear seat cushion reference point to the front-seat back in the SAE/industry standard seating test with the front seat set for a 95th-percentile driver.
assumptions: 900 mm represents a competitive-class benchmark based on current market measurements; final target will be validated against competitor data during program definition.
Measurement uses an agreed industry-standard method for knee clearance.
uncertainties: Actual packaging choices (battery for hybrids, wheelbase variants, or optional equipment) may reduce achievable legroom on some trims.

drafts.title: Accessible 12 V power socket in the trunk for portable coolers and accessories
drafts.description: Customers can plug a cooler or similar accessory into a consumer 12 V socket located in the trunk without removing cargo.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A 12 V socket is installed in the trunk, accessible without removing typical cargo, and delivers up to 12 V at 10 A (120 W) in accessory or engine-off accessory mode per vehicle electrical architecture.
assumptions: Vehicle electrical architecture supports an accessory power feed to the trunk and allows up to 10 A draw without harming starting battery in normal use.
Socket location is reachable with common cooler cable lengths.
uncertainties: Continuous high-power draws while the vehicle is parked may trigger battery-protection strategies limiting available power.

drafts.title: Request for front-end compliance with new EU pedestrian protection regulation
drafts.description: Customers asked that the vehicle front end meets the new EU pedestrian protection regulation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request: front end design complies with the new EU pedestrian protection regulation in applicable markets.
drafts.scope_reason: This is a regulation / homologation requirement requested by customers; regulatory compliance and certification planning are out of scope for a customer-facing product requirement.

drafts.title: Request that rear-seat airbags obtain FMVSS 208 certification
drafts.description: Customers asked that the rear-seat airbag system be certified to FMVSS 208.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request: rear-seat airbag system meets FMVSS 208 certification in applicable markets.
drafts.scope_reason: This is a regulatory / certification request; certification is out of scope for customer-facing product requirements.

drafts.title: Request that headlights follow ECE R112 beam rules in all markets
drafts.description: Customers asked that the headlight beam pattern conforms to ECE R112 in every market.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request: headlights conform to ECE R112 beam pattern rules where applicable.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory requirement request; homologation and market-specific beam compliance are out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Request for a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder for the volume knob (engineering spec)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the volume knob uses a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder (specific component / resolution wish).
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request: volume knob uses a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder.
drafts.scope_reason: This is a request for a specific component and resolution (engineering specification); component-level specs are out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Request for 4.5 mm laminated side windows (engineering spec)
drafts.description: Customers asked that side windows use 4.5 mm thick laminated glass.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request: side windows use 4.5 mm laminated glass.
drafts.scope_reason: This is a request for a specific glass thickness (engineering specification); component-level specifications are out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Request for seat cushion foam density of 55 kg/m³ (engineering spec)
drafts.description: Customers asked that seat cushions be made from foam with a density of 55 kg per cubic meter.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request: seat cushion foam density of 55 kg/m³.
drafts.scope_reason: This is a material/engineering specification; specific material densities are out of scope for customer-facing product requirements.

drafts.title: Request for residual value guarantee of 60% after five years (pricing / commercial)
drafts.description: Customers asked that BMW guarantees a residual value of 60% after five years.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request: residual value guarantee of 60% after five years.
drafts.scope_reason: This is a commercial/price guarantee request (residual value) and is out of scope for product feature requirements.

drafts.title: Request that BMW cut production cost per car by 8% (business / cost target)
drafts.description: Customers asked BMW to reduce production cost per car by 8 percent.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer request: production cost per car reduced by 8% compared to current baseline.
drafts.scope_reason: This is a production cost / business target request and is out of scope for product feature requirements.
